review_target: server/internal/service/access.go + access_test.go (25 leaf AccessService test cases across 15 top-level funcs, 2 with subtests) — litmus-testing the implementer's round-2 claim that all 4 design-mode findings (test-reviewer-design-1.json) were addressed, plus a fresh pass over TDD Anchor / acceptance-criteria coverage in tasks/2.md.
summary: All four claims in the round-2 report check out against the actual file, not just the summary. (1) The SetAccess/GetUser race is documented at access.go:179-185 with a comment that names both required elements: no transaction across the calls ('транзакции здесь нет') and has_access staying the authoritative source of truth ('источник истины has_access (Decision 3)'), plus the concrete consequence (a request created between GetUser and DecideRequest is left permanently pending, invisible to admin lists, but does not affect actual access) — this is exactly recommendation (a) from the design round. (2) getCalls == 0 is now asserted in all three of the SetAccess tests the round-2 report names: TestAccessService_SetAccess_Grant_SetsFlagAndApprovesRequestWithDecidedBy (line 447-449), TestAccessService_SetAccess_Revoke_UnsetsFlagAndRejectsRequest (line 483-485), TestAccessService_SetAccess_NoExistingRequest_DoesNotCallDecideRequest (line 526-528) — the 'never re-reads AccessRequestRepository' behavior is now a locked-in invariant, not an implicit fact. (3) Counted TestAccessService_InvalidArguments_ReturnErrInvalidArgumentWithoutRepoCalls by hand: exactly 10 subtests, and the whitespace gap from the design round is closed — GetAccessState, CreateRequest, and SetAccess (login) each now have both an empty-string and a whitespace-only subtest, plus SetAccess gets both an empty and a whitespace decidedBy subtest; only EnsureUser had this before. (4) The ListUsers/GetRequest scope question was correctly left as a forward note rather than fixed here — Task 2's own 'What to do' list doesn't ask for a ListUsers passthrough, and the interface signatures are fixed by tech-spec's Data Models section, so resolving 'is GetRequest ever called by a handler' is legitimately Task 4/5's concern, not this task's. Ran the full suite for real via `docker run --rm --network host -v .../server:/app -w /app golang:1.25-alpine go test ./internal/service/... -v -count=1`: all tests pass, zero failures. Counted 25 AccessService leaf tests (13 standalone + 2 subtests of TestAccessService_CreateRequest_UserAlreadyHasAccess_ReturnsErrConflictWithoutRepoCall + 10 subtests of TestAccessService_InvalidArguments_ReturnErrInvalidArgumentWithoutRepoCalls) plus the 5 pre-existing TestCostingService_* tests (CalculateInChat_UsesExpandedPricingModel, CalculateInChat_RespectsMinimumMarginFloor, CreateDeleteRestoreChat, CalculateInChat_UnknownOperation, CalculateInChat_QuickMode) — all 5 pass, no regressions. Cross-checked all 10 TDD Anchor items from tasks/2.md against the test file: all present, all with substantive state/call-count assertions (not just err==nil), none weakened. Cross-checked all 9 acceptance criteria in tasks/2.md: all satisfied (Decision 10 admin-without-flag, CreateRequest short-circuit without repo call, RowsAffected-zero-to-ErrConflict translation via stub contract, SetAccess grant/revoke with decided_by, SetAccess skips DecideRequest with no request row, ErrNotFound for unknown login, ErrForbidden/ErrConflict declared in costing.go:17-18 alongside ErrInvalidArgument/ErrNotFound, full suite green, costing_test.go untouched and passing). Litmus test result: PASS. No blocking or new findings — the round-1 full review confirms round-2's fixes are real, complete, and accurately described; nothing shallow or missing remains after two rounds.
